scopeNote: This file covers a high-confidence, well-documented starting set (California, Texas, North Carolina, Florida, Georgia, Illinois) — NOT all ~30 states that have some form of damage cap. Remaining states are a disclosed follow-up research task, not silently omitted as if they don't exist. calc-engine.js must not assume a state has no cap just because it has no entry here — that distinction (researched-and-confirmed-no-cap vs. not-yet-researched) matters and isn't encoded in the data yet.

caps.note: MICRA cap, reformed by AB 35 (2022). Non-death med-mal noneconomic damages: started $350,000 in 2023, rises $40,000/year through 2033 (cap reaches $750,000), then +2%/year thereafter. A separate, higher schedule applies to wrongful-death med-mal claims — see the California / wrongful-death entry below. Resolve the current year's figure from the schedule at runtime, never bake a single number in at build time.

schedule.afterFinalYear: increases 2% annually starting 2034, compounding on the 2033 value

caps.note: MICRA cap for medical-malpractice wrongful-death claims specifically, reformed by AB 35 (2022) — a separate, higher schedule than the non-death med-mal cap. Started $500,000 in 2023, rises $50,000/year through 2033 (cap reaches $1,000,000), then +2%/year thereafter.

schedule.afterFinalYear: increases 2% annually starting 2034, compounding on the 2033 value

caps.note: Flat $250,000 noneconomic-damages cap per claimant against an individual provider, from the 2003 Medical Malpractice and Tort Reform Act (HB 4). NOT indexed for inflation — unlike Texas's separate wrongful-death/survival cap (see that entry), this figure has not changed since 2003.

caps.note: Separate cap under Texas Civil Practice & Remedies Code § 74.303 for wrongful-death/survival med-mal claims. Base figure ($500,000 in 1977 dollars) IS indexed to the U.S. Consumer Price Index and adjusted periodically — currently over $2,000,000. Resolve the current indexed figure at runtime rather than hardcoding a value that will go stale.

schedule.note: CPI-indexed from a $500,000 (1977) base — exact current figure needs a fresh CPI-adjustment lookup at build/runtime, not hardcoded here

caps.note: Noneconomic damages cap, originally $500,000 (2011), adjusted for inflation every 3 years per G.S. § 90-21.19 — most recent adjustment effective January 1, 2026 set it at $712,847. Does NOT apply where the provider's conduct was reckless/malicious/intentional/grossly negligent AND caused disfigurement, permanent injury, loss of body function, or death — those cases are uncapped. Next scheduled adjustment: January 1, 2029.

caps.note: Florida's tiered noneconomic-damages caps for medical malpractice were struck down by the Florida Supreme Court in North Broward Hospital District v. Kalitan (2017) on equal-protection grounds. No cap currently applies to Florida med-mal noneconomic damages — this entry exists so the page can state that accurately (a cap existed, it no longer applies), not to silently omit the topic.

sources.name: LegalMatch — Constitutionality of Medical Malpractice Damage Caps

caps.note: Georgia's $350,000 noneconomic-damages cap was struck down by the Georgia Supreme Court in Atlanta Oculoplastic Surgery, P.C. v. Nestlehutt (2010) as violating the right to jury trial. No cap currently applies.

sources.name: LegalMatch — Constitutionality of Medical Malpractice Damage Caps

caps.note: Illinois's caps ($500,000 for individual physicians, $1,000,000 for hospitals) were struck down by the Illinois Supreme Court in Lebron v. Gottlieb Memorial Hospital (Feb. 4, 2010) as violating separation of powers. No cap currently applies.
